phase_name: Authority Evaluation Integration Contract Independent Verification
summary: Phase 147L was authorized, following Phase 147K's AUTHORITY EVALUATION INTEGRATION CONTRACT FROZEN verdict, to independently verify AESIC-001 v1.0 -- verification-only, no implementation, no contract amendment, no schema change, no runtime change. This phase independently reconstructed the integration architecture from primary sources -- AEM-001 v1.0, AEMIC-001 v1.2, direct inspection of the current src/pcae/authority_evaluation/{__init__,models,evaluation,registry,errors,serialization}.py source, and requirement-ID-anchored excerpts of IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, and CHGR-001 (with the actual coordinator.py, storage.py, and record.py source those citations reference directly re-read to confirm every code-level claim) -- deliberately before re-deriving AESIC-001's own architectural conclusions in detail. The independent reconstruction converged on the same architecture AESIC-001 freezes: a dedicated Authority Evaluation Service (AES) as sole reader of Session.owner_identity, sole resolver of Decision Templates and Registry declarations, sole invoker of the unmodified, pure evaluate(), running at two timing points with Stage 2 unconditionally superseding Stage 1; no component-boundary, ownership, or no-amendment claim in AESIC-001 was contradicted. All 117 AESIC-REQ requirements were then classified against the reconstruction, direct source inspection, or cited predecessor-contract text in a complete requirement verification matrix. Two Major, non-blocking internal-consistency findings were identified by direct textual analysis of AESIC-001 against itself: (1) stage_1_outcome_ref (AESIC-REQ-057, section 8.6) is defined to make both outcomes retrievable, but Stage 1's outcome is separately and unconditionally guaranteed never to be persisted anywhere (AESIC-REQ-064/080, sections 9.1/12.2) -- a reference cannot make a value retrievable when the same contract forbids that value from ever being durably stored; (2) Stage 2's idempotency mechanism (AESIC-REQ-019, mirroring an O_CREAT|O_EXCL exclusive-create, one-record-per-package_id store) structurally cannot accommodate section 11.2's own restart-matrix rows (Registry evolution, Decision Template evolution), which require a changed-input retry to produce a genuinely different, disclosed outcome as a new record under the same key that a strict exclusive-create store can only refuse, not supersede. One Minor finding (an unspecified equality procedure for AESIC-REQ-023(a)'s inputs-unchanged idempotency check, compounded by AESIC-REQ-102's performance budget omitting the implied AER-store read) and one Informational finding (the relationship between evaluation_id and stage_1_outcome_ref is never stated) were also recorded. Adversarial attack sections (replay, persistence, failure ownership, security, observability, threat analysis) attempted to construct additional failures against both the reconstruction and AESIC-001's own text; no Blocking finding, unsupported requirement, or predecessor-contract contradiction was found beyond the two Major findings already named. Cross-contract compatibility (AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, CHGR-001, all six confirmed requiring zero amendment, per AESIC-REQ-113) was independently reconfirmed by direct citation-checking rather than accepting AESIC-001's own compatibility claims, including direct verification that the codebase's actual _PROHIBITED_PACKAGE_FIELDS frozenset in coordinator.py does not conflict with the proposed authority_evaluation_ref readiness-package field. Overall Verdict: AESIC-001 VERIFIED WITH NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS. Full detail in docs/verification/PHASE_147L_AUTHORITY_EVALUATION_INTEGRATION_CONTRACT_INDEPENDENT_VERIFICATION.md.

validation_results.name: phase_147l_independent_reconstruction
validation_results.result: Independently reconstructed orchestration ownership, evaluator ownership, the Registry boundary, Decision Template Resolution boundary, Session ownership, Publication ownership, CHGR interaction, replay architecture, persistence architecture, lifecycle sequencing, failure ownership, and disclosure-only semantics from AEM-001/AEMIC-001/direct source inspection/predecessor-contract citations alone, deliberately before re-deriving AESIC-001's own architectural conclusions in detail. The reconstruction converged on AESIC-001's own architecture with no contradiction found -- documented in section 2 of the deliverable, with every conclusion's basis cited.

validation_results.name: phase_147l_requirement_verification_matrix
validation_results.result: All 117 AESIC-REQ-### requirements classified against the independent reconstruction, direct source-code inspection, or cited predecessor-contract text. 113 of 117 Independently Supported or Contract-Supported with no qualification beyond cross-referencing; 1 Ambiguous (Minor, Finding 3); 3 directly implicated in two Internally Inconsistent (Major) findings (REQ-023, REQ-057, REQ-078/080 jointly, Findings 1-2). Zero requirements found Unsupported, improperly Redundant, or contradicted by a predecessor contract.

validation_results.name: phase_147l_adversarial_sections
validation_results.result: Performed adversarial attacks against lifecycle sequencing, replay (seven attack scenarios including duplicate/inconsistent/stale/partial/cross-session replay and replay after Registry/template evolution), persistence (AER identity, digest ownership, immutable/transient state, cross-artifact references, completeness), failure ownership (ownership/retry/logging/recovery/user-visible-ambiguity checks against every matrix row), security (nine named threats individually attacked), observability, and a fresh, AESIC-001-text-blind threat enumeration compared against section 15's own table. Two Major findings constructed (replay attack items 2/6/7, persistence-completeness check); no additional Blocking or Major finding constructed beyond those two.

validation_results.name: phase_147l_cross_contract_compatibility_verification
validation_results.result: Independently re-confirmed AESIC-001's citations of AEM-REQ-003/010/014/037, AEMIC-REQ-019/073/074/075/076/107, IWC-REQ-026/036/037, IWPC-REQ-144/147, PEC-REQ-113/115/116, and CHGR-REQ-096/097/199/207/208 are all accurate by direct line-anchored re-reading, not merely accepted from AESIC-001's own text. Directly re-read coordinator.py's actual _PROHIBITED_PACKAGE_FIELDS frozenset (five members: chgr_id, publication_state, publication_result, authority_token, execution_state) confirming no collision with the proposed authority_evaluation_ref readiness-package reference field, and record.py's actual _RECORD_ID_PREFIX_BY_FAMILY dict confirming no prefix collision with the proposed authority_evaluation_record family. Zero amendments required to AEM-001, AEMIC-001, IWC-001, IWPC-001, PEC-001, or CHGR-001, independently reconfirming AESIC-REQ-113.
